findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed seal of walk-in cooler to be damaged. Observed caulking around dish sink to be in need of replacement. Caulking was cracked and damaged. Informed PIC that repairs need to be made, and she took note to contact maintenance. Ensure facilities are in good repair to promote clean food prep spaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Observed ground beef being thawed on counter at room temperature. PIC stated that ground beef had only been removed from walk-in freezer a few minutes previous. Ground beef was placed in walk-in cooler during inspection. 

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 
Observed the edges of counter tops at the pass through window in the dish room and the edge of counter top pass through behind the steam well to be in disrepair. The floor is also in disrepair with deep groves and gaps. There is a plan to replace and they are waiting on more information to do bids for food service while the kitchen is shut down for flooring removal and installation.  Correct violations for next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-602.12: (A) Observed interior of microwave in kitchen to be soiled with food debris.  The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-602.11: (A) Observed blade of can opener in kitchen to be soiled with food debris.  FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (A) Sanitizer used by facility was not able to be tested with chlorine or quat strips.  Had facility switch to bleach sanitizer.  Facility has bleach test strips. Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.
Wet wiping cloth is observed to be sitting on the prep table. Cloth was placed back into the proper bucket.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12. Observed employee to recontaminate hands with papertowel that was used to turn off faucet at hand sink.  Dispose of towel directly after turning off faucet handle.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14. findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: 4-202.11  (Pf) Food-Contact surface of red plastic bowl is no longer smooth and easily cleanable. Bowl was immediatly discarded. A food-contact surface that is not smooth and easily cleanable can harbor bacteria that con be transfer to food. Replace with a National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI approved surface. Reference 4-202.11.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces of cardboard boxes used for storage of cheese in the walk in and other food storage in the dry storage room are not easily cleanable. Replace cardboard boxes with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: Chemical sanitizer in the dish machine tested at 0ppm of chlorine. The container was almost empty and the color of the liquid was very clear verses having a yellow tone as with new/fresh solution. A new bucket was added and the machine tested out properly. 750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: Observed cloth used for cleaning tables to be stored on the bottle of cleaner in the dining room. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. Store cloths properly between uses. Cloth was removed to the laundry as is the standard practice.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Sliced brownies for lunch service were observed uncovered in bowls on serving trays. Brownies were sliced before 930a; lunch would not be served until 11a. Staff covered the brownies with parchment paper. Keep foods covered until food service begins to protect items from potential contamination.

Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
750.140b - Turkey cooling in the walkin cooler was observed with surface and internal temperatures of 74F-77F and 101F-115F respectively. The container was sealed, and the lid had condensation buildup on the inner surface. Today's date was marked on the container, but no time was indicated. Manager stated the turkey was cooked this morning, shredded, and then held hot in the oven until it was placed in the steam table for lunch. The turkey was pulled from the steam table around 1245p and placed in the walkin cooler. Temperature was initially checked around 145p. Benefit of doubt was given, and the turkey was placed on an ice bath with the lid off in the walkin freezer to help quickly drop the temperature of the product. Manager checked the internal temperature around 230p, and the turkey was at 73F. Manager was advised to continue monitoring the temperature throughout the cooling process.

Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6 hrs. Monitor the time and temperature during the cooling process to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frame required for proper cooling. Mark the date and time on cooling foods.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Open gallon of milk in walkin cooler did not have a date mark but was believed to have been opened the day prior. Based on information provided and the amount of product remaining (~3/4 full), benefit of doubt was given. Milk was dated and kept for use.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous food must be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Carrots in steam table had surface and internal temperatures ranging from 94F-116F. Cook stated the carrots started out frozen and were temporarily placed in the steam table to speed up thawing process prior to cooking in the oven. Carrots were immediately removed from steam table and placed in oven to finish cooking. Options for proper thawing were discussed (either in walkin cooler overnight, under cold running water, or as part of the cooking process). **NOTE: the steam table is only intended to hold foods hot after they have been properly cooked or reheated using equipment intended for such (i.e. oven, stove). Do not use the steam table for heating or thawing potentially hazardous foods**
  
Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the following methods: 1. under refrigeration 41F/below, 2. under potable running water 70F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. in microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. as part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.160 - Cook touched door knob to kitchen door and did not change gloves before returning to prep area. Proper glove use and handwashing between glove changes were discussed.
Cook washed hands and put on a new pair of gloves prior to continuing with food prep.

Gloves shall be single use and used for only one task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Damp wiping cloth was observed with RTU spray in dining area. Wiping cloth was placed in soiled linen container in dish area. Wiping cloths must be stored in a sanitizer solution between uses. Use disposable paper towels with sanitizer spray.
**If staff prefer the cloth towel with the spray, then make sure the wiping cloth is used for one round of wiping all the tables at once. Then the wiping cloth must be placed in the soiled linen storage container. A new wiping cloth must be used every time tables are wiped and immediately placed in soiled linen storage.**

In-use wet wiping cloths must be stored in a sanitizer solution between uses.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 160 - A) Employee went between tasks without changing gloves - rinsing a soiled pan in dish area to retrieving plastic wrap at the food prep table. After changing gloves the employee was observed touching unclean surfaces (trash can lid) and his person (crossing arms/touching shirt and upper arms) and then gloves remained on hands. Gloves were discarded at the request of inspector. Proper glove use was discussed.

Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.

B) Employee was observed washing hands without use of proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without use of paper towels as a barrier. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Hands were re-washed using proper technique.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food, clean equipment, or unwrapped single service articles. Hands must also be washed before putting on gloves, between glove changes, and upon entering the kitchen and before beginning tasks related to food and food related items (clean equipment, single service articles).

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Metal rod at water dispenser had buildup along the bottom edge (lime and possibly the beginnings of pink mold).

Clean and sanitize the metal rod of the water dispenser as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.
**Metal rod was cleaned and sanitized during inspection**

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Facility test strips indicated the concentration of the Redi San RTU Hard Surface Sanitizer was at 100ppm. However, inspector's test strips showed the concentration of Redi San at 200ppm. Quat test strips available for use had expiration date of October 2014. Expired test strips were discarded. Inspector provided some test strips to replace those that were discarded until new set could be purchased (Manager kept container and ppm chart for comparison).

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - Dust accumulation was observed on wires and chemical lines on the back side and underneath dish machine. Dust was also noted on the drain line of the dish machine. Clean the aforementioned areas of the dish machine. 

Non-food contact surfaces shall be cleaned daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris and maintained clean.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Cooked sausage in walkin cooler had surface temperature of 42F and internal temperature ranging from 46F-50F. When foil was moved heavy condensation was noted inside. Employee noted the sausage was placed in the walkin cooler around 10a. The cover was labeled with the date but not the time. Benefit of doubt was given; product was stirred and foil removed for the duration of the cooling process. Proper cooling was discussed with employee.
Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F. (see general comments)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The top and back side of the dish machine were soiled. Heavy dust accumulation was noted on the back of the machine, especially on wires and chemical lines. Clean the top and back of the dish machine, focusing effort on areas with heavy dust accumulation.
Non-food contact surfaces shall be cleaned daily/as needed and maintained clean.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 Floor in walkin cooler had some debris under back shelving, and puddling water was observed in the back left corner. Clean the floor under walkin cooler shelves daily/as needed and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.citation_text:
750.1390 - Damp mop was observed stored with head down on the floor in the dish room. Mop was hung up on the wall mounted storage rack during the inspection. Store wet mops hanging or inverted to allow for proper drying. 
Maintenance and cleaning tools shall be maintained and stored properly.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750.130d - Flats of raw shell eggs and a box of raw bacon were observed above ready to eat foods (boxes of tortilla shells and juice) in the walkin cooler. Raw and ready to eat foods were rearranged so ready to eat foods were separated from raw products. All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or away from raw foods.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.850 & 860 - Utensils stored in a coffee cup were noted to have food surfaces extended up. Utensils were rearranged so handles were extended up out of the cup. Store utensils in containers with handles extended up out of containers to avoid contact with cleaned/sanitized food contact surfaces when utensils are being retrieved. 
Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.
Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - Puddling water was observed in walkin cooler under the shelves to the left of the door. Manager noted there is an issue with condensation at the shared wall between the walkin freezer and walkin cooler. Staff clean the floor as needed, but a call for service will be made to R & W Refrigeration to further address the issue. Floors shall be kept clean. Mop up the condensation from the walkin cooler floor as needed to eliminate puddling water until repairs have been made to eliminate the issue with condensation.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750.140b - Container of cooked taco chicken meat in walkin freezer had a surface temperature of 56F and an internal temperature range of 88F - 103F. Container was tightly sealed and no time was written. Employee stated he did not know the temperature of the food when it was placed in the cooler approximately 1hr and 20 minutes earlier. Product was discarded. Changes for cooling process were discussed. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in 4 hrs. (see general comments)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) crevice around sprayer surface (buildup); B) side of stove next to wall (dust buildup); C) tray holding spices in dry storage room; & D) container holding whipped spread packets (crumbs/debris). Clean all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Linoleum floor was observed to be cracked in the dish room along the wall on the left side of the dish machine and on the floor to the left of the prep sink. The aforementioned areas need to be properly sealed so they are smooth, easily cleanable, and do not provide potential hiding places for pests. B) The floors were observed to be soiled in the following areas: 1) walkin freezer (along walls/in corners); 2) walkin cooler (on right side under shelves); 3) dry storage under shelves; & 4) under stoves (dust, debris, and old glue trap). Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 & 1220 - A) Counter on left side of dish machine was missing chunks of silicone and pulling away from the wall. Re-seal the counter to the wall. B) Caulk at sprayer sink was moldy and needs to be replaced. Also, wall below sprayer sink counter was moldy and needs to be cleaned. Clean and re-caulk the aforementioned areas of the sprayer sink. C) Wall by handsink has small holes and covering has torn off. Fill the holes and re-seal the wall so it is smooth and easily cleanable. **Check walls throughout and fill any and all holes**. D) Wall next to stove had some dust accumulation. Clean the wall by the stove.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Attic frame is loose at the top of ceiling area--ceiling vent in dry storage area with rust buildup and dust buildup.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed dust  on the ceiling near the vent over the prep table.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Absence of labeling and dating on sliced cheese and bag of cheese that is opened
All foods not stored in their original container must be properly labeled with the common name, date, and time in order to help ensure proper handling and reduce the potential of cross contamination.  Properly label all foods.
